newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $65, passed -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $65, passed -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Thursday were bid $65.00 per cwt and passed by owners who priced cattle at $66.00, feedlot sources said.

Active sales Wednesday at $65.00 were $1.00 higher than last week. Feedlot cattle prices the remainder of the week were seen steady to firm amid ideas that strong beef demand would keep packer buying interest strong, they said.

Several pens of cattle that were sold Wednesday in the Texas Panhandle were shipped early Thursday, one feedlot manager said. The quick shipments reflected how short some packers were on live inventories, the manager said.
Beef prices Wednesday were quoted up $0.07 to $0.27 per cwt, with lightweight choice up $0.27 at $96.51, USDA said. There were 215 fabricated beef loads sold.
Fed cattle prices also were underpinned by light cattle weights compared with a year ago, and by lower showlist numbers compared with last week, the feedlot sources said.

Average weights for the week ended February 15 were estimated at 1,163 lbs, compared with 1,164 lbs the previous week and an actual 1,177 lbs a year ago, USDA statistics showed. Weights were down because feedlots have marketed aggressively and ahead of schedule, the sources said.
